description: Cities, situated at the crossroads of rising temperatures and growing populations, bear the brunt of climate change and must adapt to the new normal of extreme weather impacts. Today, we face both a unique opportunity and a timely responsibility to implement urban design interventions and adaptation strategies that will equip cities to withstand the impacts of climate change in the coming century. Our lab focuses on exploring innovative urban design and climate adaptation strategies to combat the growing threat of extreme heat, especially in rapidly developing cities.
hero_image_alt: Research at The Urban Planet Lab
section_description: We study how extreme heat emerges within cities, who it affects most, and how cities can adapt. Bringing together complexity science, urban climate modeling, and thermal remote sensing, our work spans a set of connected themes—and the projects below show how we put them into practice.
closing_statement: Our work is supported by various funding agencies such as NASA and NYU internal grants.
